'''''Star Wars: Andor''''', alternatively titled '''''Andor''''' and later marketed as '''''Andor: A Star Wars Story''''' for the second season, is an American [[Wikipedia:Live-action|live-action]] [[Wikipedia:Television_show|television series]] developed by [[Lucasfilm]] and released on [[Disney+]]. The series is a [[spy]] thriller starring [[Diego Luna]], reprising his role as [[Cassian Jeron Andor|Cassian Andor]] from the [[2016]] film ''[[Rogue One: A Star Wars Story]]''. The [[Andor Season 1|first season]] premiered in [[September]] [[2022]], and the [[Andor Season 2|second season]] premiered on [[April 22]], [[2025]] with a new logo.

==Official description==
''The ''Andor'' series will explore a new perspective from the ''Star Wars'' galaxy, focusing on Cassian Andor's journey to discover the difference he can make. The series brings forward the tale of the burgeoning rebellion against the Empire and how people and planets became involved. It's an era filled with danger, deception and intrigue where Cassian will embark on the path that is destined to turn him into a rebel hero.<ref name="Media kit" />''

==Development==
====Announcement====
{{Quote|Going back to the ''Star Wars'' universe is very special for me. I have so many memories of the great work we did together and the relationships I made throughout the journey. We have a fantastic adventure ahead of us, and this new exciting format will give us the chance to explore this character more deeply.|Diego Luna, on reprising his role|<ref name="Announcement" />}}
Talks for a television series focused on [[Cassian Jeron Andor]], [[Diego Luna]]'s character from the [[2016]] [[Star Wars Anthology Series|''Star Wars'' Anthology]] film ''[[Rogue One: A Star Wars Story]]'', began before the Anthology film was released, though Luna had doubts that it would happen.<ref>{{IMDb|url=video/vi1766702873?listId=ls025849840|text=Diego Luna Knows How to Play an Authentic Villain and Raise a Future Jedi|archivedate=20200424211503}}</ref> In [[February]] [[2018]], Disney CEO [[Bob Iger (chief executive officer)|Bob Iger]] revealed that "a few" ''Star Wars'' live-action series were in development for [[Disney+|Disney's streaming service]].<ref>{{WebCite|url=https://www.hollywoodreporter.com/live-feed/star-wars-tv-series-disney-developing-a-few-streaming-service-1082523|text='Star Wars' TV Series: Disney Developing "a Few" for Its Streaming Service|author=Lesley Goldberg, Aaron Couch|date=2018-02-06|work=[[Wikipedia:The Hollywood Reporter|''The Hollywood Reporter'']]|archivedate=20200307153245}}</ref> The series was officially announced by Iger during a Disney quarterly earnings call on [[November 8]], 2018.<ref name="Announcement" />

[[File:Andor_Promotional_Banner.png|thumb|right|250px|A promotional banner for the series]]
On [[November 30]], it was reported that [[Wikipedia:The Americans (2013 TV series)|''The Americans'']] executive producer [[Stephen Schiff]] was tapped to serve as a showrunner while [[Wikipedia:Moana (2016 film)|''Moana'']] writer [[Wikipedia:Jared Bush|Jared Bush]] was revealed to have originated the project by writing a pilot script and a [[Wikipedia:Bible (screenwriting)|series bible]].<ref name="Schiff & Bush">{{WebCite|url=https://deadline.com/2018/11/star-wars-series-diego-luna-taps-stephen-schiff-showrunner-disney-plus-streaming-1202511875|text=Disney+ 'Star Wars' Series Starring Diego Luna Taps Stephen Schiff As Showrunner|author=Nellie Andreeva|date=2018-11-30|work=[[Wikipedia:Deadline Hollywood|''Deadline'']]|archivedate=20200403054007}}</ref> According to [https://www.productionweekly.com Production Weekly], the series was scheduled to begin production in October [[2019]].<ref name="Filming Scheduled Date">{{WebCite|url=http://www.theforce.net/story/front/Rogue_One_Series_Has_A_Filming_Date_182809.asp|text=Rogue One Series Has A Filming Date|author=Steve Dunk|date=2018-12-31|work=[[TheForce.net]]|archivedate=20190729234037}}</ref> On [[July 11]], 2019, [[Rick Famuyiwa]] was reported to be in talks to direct an undisclosed amount of episodes for the series, with filming scheduled to begin on [[October 7]].<ref>{{WebCite|url=https://discussingfilm.net/2019/07/11/rick-famuyiwa-in-talks-to-direct-episodes-of-cassian-andor-series-exclusive|text=Rick Famuyiwa In Talks To Direct Episodes Of Cassian Andor Series (EXCLUSIVE)|author=Jacob Fisher|date=2019-07-11|work=[https://discussingfilm.net DiscussingFilm]|archivedate=20200407112233}}</ref> On October 15, 2019, Variety reported that ''Rogue One'' co-writer [[Tony Gilroy]] would be writing the pilot for the series in addition to directing multiple episodes.<ref>{{WebCite|url=https://variety.com/2019/tv/news/cassian-andor-series-tony-gilroy-diego-luna-disney-plus-1203370479|text='Rogue One' Writer Tony Gilroy Joins Cassian Andor 'Star Wars' Series at Disney Plus (EXCLUSIVE)|author=Joe Otterson|date=2019-10-15|work=[[Wikipedia:Variety (magazine)|''Variety'']]|archivedate=20200403065859}}</ref>

Lucasfilm's original concept for the series focused on the adventures of Andor and his reprogrammed [[KX-series security droid]], [[K-2SO]], who is played by [[Alan Tudyk]]. The two would have a [[Wikipedia:Butch Cassidy and the Sundance Kid|Butch and Sundance]] style dynamic, with the two set to storm a citadel<ref name="Real People">{{WebCite|url=https://variety.com/2022/tv/news/star-wars-andor-tony-gilroy-diego-luna-1235348148|text=How ‘Andor' Became the First ‘Star Wars' TV Series for Grown-Ups: ‘I Wanted to Do It About Real People'|author=Vary, Adam B|work=[[Wikipedia:Variety (magazine)|''Variety'']]|archivedate=20220824140042}}</ref> in the series pilot.<ref name="Controversial Story">{{WebCite|url=https://www.slashfilm.com/1857713/andor-showrunner-tony-gilroy-most-controversial-storyline-explained|text=Andor Showrunner Tony Gilroy Addresses The Series' Most Controversial Storyline [Exclusive Interview]|author=Pearson, Ben|work=''Slash Film''|archivedate=20250515031238}}</ref> Thanks to his work on ''Rogue One'', Gilroy was consulted for work on the prequel series.<ref name="TimesUnion">{{WebCite|url=https://www.timesunion.com/hudsonvalley/culture/article/tony-gilroy-andor-star-wars-profile-20326721.php|text=Tony Gilroy’s journey from the Hudson Valley to a galaxy far, far away|author=Gregory James Wakeman|work=''Times Union''|archivedate=20250519195229}}</ref> He thought the original pitch was "fine" but felt it was "very hard to sustain over a long haul,"<ref name="Real People" /> questioning what they could do after storming a citadel at the show's very start. Furthermore, he knew from his experience on ''Rogue One'' that K-2SO was a hard character to work with for long periods of time, which would make an entire series starring the character difficult, lest Lucasfilm wanted to have to find ways to hide him during many missions.<ref name="Controversial Story" />

[[File:Andor1-Cassiankillsguard.png|thumb|left|300px|Tony Gilroy's pitch for ''Andor'' took the character of Cassian Andor back five years and followed him into "the worst night of his life."]]
Without outright saying he was interested, Gilroy responded with what was later called "a long forensic manifesto" to Lucasfilm, outlining his issues with the pitch and putting forth his own ideas. Gilroy's idea was the story that would become ''Andor'',<ref name="Real People" /> pitching a story that took Andor himself "back five years, to the worst night of his life." In the process, the series would see Andor evolve into the man first seen in ''Rogue One''. According to Gilroy, Lucasfilm thought his pitch "looked a little insane,"<ref name="TimesUnion" /> and he fully admitted the story he had in mind was "a crazy idea" and "radical."<ref name="Real People" /> In the end, however, Lucasfilm decided Gilroy's story was the route to go.<ref name="TimesUnion" />

====Gilroy's concepts====
=====Overview=====
{{Expandsect}}
As far back as his pitch to Lucasfilm, Gilroy, as a student of history, wanted to imbue the series with themes of revolution, fascism, politics, rebellion, and the regular people caught up on those conflicts.<ref name="TimesUnion" /> When Gilroy was asked about political resonances in ''Andor'' in November 2022, he stated that the series was written without contemporary politics in mind, drawing on historical revolutions simply as spontaneous events to drive the characters' adventures—"whatever contemporary resonance it has is usually in the eye of the beholder. Oppression is oppression."<ref name="Oppression">{{WebCite|url=https://www.indiewire.com/features/general/andor-not-political-disney-plus-tony-gilroy-interview-1234780620|text='Andor': Tony Gilroy's 'Star Wars' Series Wasn't Meant to be Political|author=Proma Khosla|date=2022-11-09|work=[[Wikipedia:IndieWire|''IndieWire'']]|archivedate=20230518200016}}</ref> In another November interview, Gilroy emphasized that his personal politics are "absolutely not important" to the series' themes and that ''Star Wars'' allows plentiful comparisons to history. As to the "age old question" of "who's a terrorist and who's a freedom fighter," Gilroy wanted every character to "speak for themselves" to make their motives believable and referred the idea of controversial revolutionaries to historical nation-building movements, naming the United States' [[Wikipedia:Thomas Jefferson|Thomas Jefferson]] and South Africa [[Wikipedia:Nelson Mandela|Nelson Mandela]] and further listing the revolutions of France, [[Wikipedia:Haiti|Haiti]], [[Wikipedia:October Revolution|Russia and the Soviet Union]], and the nation-building of Israel.<ref name="Themes">{{WebCite|url=https://nerdist.com/article/andor-showrunner-tony-gilroy-interview-season-one-themes-hope-community-cassian-future|text=ANDOR Showrunner Tony Gilroy on Season 1's Powerful Themes and the Future|author=Michael Walsh|date=2022-11-23|work=[[Wikipedia:Nerdist|Nerdist]]|archivedate=20221123110025}}</ref> The [[Rix Road (episode)|season one finale]] took inspiration from the 1966 [[Wikipedia:Gillo Pontecorvo|Gillo Pontecorvo]] film [[Wikipedia:The Battle of Algiers|''The Battle of Algiers'']], which was based on the [[Wikipedia:Algerian War|Algerian War of Independence]] against the colonial [[Wikipedia:French Fourth Republic|French government]].<ref name="Algiers">{{WebCite|url=https://www.hollywoodreporter.com/movies/movie-features/sharper-director-benjamin-caron-apple-movie-andor-1235356365|text=Sharper Director Benjamin Caron Talks Twisty Apple Movie, Andor|author=Brian Davids|date=2023-03-20|work=[[Wikipedia:The Hollywood Reporter|The Hollywood Reporter]]|archivedate=20230320182210}}</ref>

Gilroy also likened ''Andor''{{'s}} character of [[Luthen Rael]] as a [[Wikipedia:Startup company|start-up company]] founder<ref name="Themes" /> and, earlier in September, identified the senator and eventual Rebel Alliance leader [[Mon Mothma]] as a "figurehead of [[Democracy|liberal democracy]] that will fail"<ref name="Mothma">{{WebCite|url=https://www.vanityfair.com/hollywood/2022/09/mon-mothma-andor-star-wars|text=Who Is Mon Mothma? Star Wars Fans Are About To Be Shocked|author=Anthony Breznican|date=2022-09-27|work=[[Wikipedia:Vanity Fair (magazine)|''Vanity Fair'']]|archiveurl=https://archive.is/NZSCB}}</ref>—he compared her to [[Wikipedia:Speaker of the United States House of Representatives|US House Speaker]] [[Wikipedia:Nancy Pelosi|Nancy Pelosi]] in another interview in the same month.<ref name="Pelosi">{{WebCite|url=https://www.indiewire.com/features/general/andor-syril-karn-mon-mothma-1234764813|text=Tony Gilroy Unpacks 'Andor' Ep. 4: Mon Mothma Is 'a Nancy Pelosi Character'|author=Proma Khosla|date=2022-09-28|work=[[Wikipedia:IndieWire|''IndieWire'']]|archivedate=20230507110140}}</ref> [[Fiona Shaw]], who played [[Maarva Carassi Andor|Maarva Andor]] and spoke in an interview released in August 2022, thought that Gilroy's story is a "scurrilous" and "[[Wikipedia:Social realism|social-realist]]" take on "the [[Wikipedia:Donald Trump|Trumpian]] world" that was "exploding in different places right now" with people's rights being taken away.<ref name="Trumpian world" />

=====Five season plan=====
{{Quote|We were halfway through shooting season 1, coming through Covid, and the monumental size of the show, the effort, and everything else was just dawning on us. We realized that I didn't have enough calories to do it, and Diego's face couldn't take the timing, because it just takes too long to make it. We were saved by Disney saying, 'Okay, if you guys can figure out a way to do it, we're into it.|Tony Gilroy, on shifting to two seasons|<ref name="Radar03-26-25">{{WebCite|url=https://www.gamesradar.com/entertainment/star-wars-tv-shows/andor-showrunner-says-season-2s-more-fast-paced-structure-is-a-fascinating-experiment-that-is-born-out-of-desperation-i-dont-know-if-anyones-ever-done-it-before|text=Andor showrunner says season 2's more fast-paced structure is a "fascinating experiment" that is "born out of desperation": "I don't know if anyone's ever done it before"|author=Russell, Bradley and Edwards, Richard|date=2025-03-26|work=''Games Radar''|archivedate=20250331024316}}</ref>}}
Originally, Gilroy thought of ''Andor'' as a five season show<ref name="Controversial Story" /> with around sixty episodes. It was during that planning phase that [[Stellan Skarsgård]], who plays Rael, joined the series, but he asked Gilroy to kill off his character at the end of season two so he did not have to stay for the entire series.<ref name="Vulture05-16-25">{{WebCite|url=https://www.vulture.com/article/tony-gilroy-andor-star-wars-rogue-one-interview.html|text=‘Before Anyone Else Defines It, I’m Going to Define It’ Andor creator Tony Gilroy reflects on five years inside the Star Wars universe|author=VanArendonk, Kathryn|date=2025-05-16|work=''Vulture''|archivedate=20250519093736}}</ref> According to Gilroy, the five season ''Andor'' had the same overall story progression as the final series.<ref name="Controversial Story" /> In the end, he would decide to pivot to just two seasons and believes that he did not lose anything major.<ref name="Backstory05-17-25">{{YouTube|video=4EWCzic9z_M|text=Andor S2 Q&A - Tony Gilroy - Season Recap|channel=backstorymagazine2757|name=Backstory Magazine|date=2025-05-17}}</ref> Gilroy reflected that he had only planned out season one by the time he was heading into a writer's room.<ref name="Controversial Story" />

As recalled by Gilroy, the decision to shift to only two seasons came halfway through season one production as the scale of the production became clear to himself and the crew.<ref name="Radar03-26-25" /> Luna feared that he would visibly age over the production of five seasons.<ref name="Popverse, 2024-07-24">{{WebCite|url=https://www.thepopverse.com/tv-star-wars-andor-season-2-3-4-5-plans-changed-diego-luna-ace-2024|text=Star Wars: Andor star Diego Luna describes how they're fitting four seasons of planned story into the second (and final) season|author=apin-Bertone, Joshua|date=2024-07-24|work=''Pop Verse''|archivedate=20240803203145}}</ref> Furthermore, Gilroy believed that there was not enough story left in ''Andor'' for twelve episodes across four more seasons.<ref name="Screenrant11-21-24">{{WebCite|url=https://screenrant.com/star-wars-andor-five-season-story|text=Andor Was Originally Pitched As A Five-Season Story, So Why Are We Only Getting Two?|author=Bacon, Thomas|date=2024-11-21|work=''Screen Rant''|archivedate=20250323194300}}</ref> As a solution, ''Andor'' was shortened to two seasons, with the second season featuring four story arcs that each covered a year of the timeline up to ''Rogue One''.<ref name="Popverse, 2024-07-24" /> In doing so, ''Andor'' fulfilled its purpose of telling a five year story. According to Gilroy, Luna and himself came to the decision together while drinking scotch.<ref name="Screenrant11-21-24" /> Luna, meanwhile, credits Gilroy for the "great idea."<ref name="Popverse, 2024-07-24" /> Gilroy considers season two "a fascinating experiment."<ref name="Radar03-26-25" />

===Production===
====Season one filming====
[[File:AndorSeries.jpg|thumb|right|250px|The original series logo revealed in 2020]]
On [[December 3]], 2020,<ref name="Kimmel Schedule">{{WebCite|url=https://abc.com/shows/jimmy-kimmel-live/news/schedule/jkl-schedule-for-11302020|text=Jimmy Kimmel Live Schedule for the Week of 11/30/2020|work=[[Wikipedia:American Broadcasting Company|ABC Entertainment]]|archivedate=20201204210812}}</ref> Diego Luna confirmed that the series had started filming in London.<ref name="Jimmy Kimmel">{{OfficialYouTube|channel=@JimmyKimmelLive|name=Jimmy Kimmel Live|video=CjApD1utCIk|text=Diego Luna on Star Wars Spin-Off, His Father Hating Christmas & Recreating The Princess Bride}}</ref> The title of ''Andor'', as well as behind the scenes footage of the filming of the series, were unveiled on [[December 10]], 2020 at a [[The Walt Disney Company|Disney]] investors meeting. Filming began in late [[November]] of 2020.<ref name="Dec 10">{{SW|url=news/future-lucasfilm-projects-revealed|text=Future Lucasfilm Projects Revealed}}</ref><ref name="Sizzle">{{SWYouTube|gSW-pARyP-M|Sizzle Reel | Andor | Disney+|sw_url=video/sizzle-andor}}</ref> Although Alan Tudyk was initially announced to play K-2SO in the series,<ref name="D23">{{SW|url=news/the-galaxy-far-far-away-just-got-a-little-bigger|text=The Galaxy Far, Far Away Just Got A Little Bigger…}}</ref> he later clarified in [[January]] of [[2021]] that while production was underway, he was not going to appear in the first season. He did, however, expect to be brought into the fold in later seasons.<ref name="NoAlan">{{WebCite|url=https://collider.com/rogue-one-cassian-andor-series-cast-k2so-absence-explained-alan-tudyk-interview|text='Rogue One' Disney+ Series Won't Include K-2SO, Alan Tudyk Confirms — At Least At First|author=Drew Taylor|date=2021-01-20|work=[[Wikipedia:Collider (website)|''Collider'']]|archivedate=20210121012631}}</ref>

The showrunners opted for practical environments, with scenes being shot at [[Pinewood Studios]] and on location. One scene was shot at [[Wikipedia:Pitlochry|Pitlochry]], [[Wikipedia:Scotland|Scotland]],<ref name="Empire">{{WebCite|url=https://www.empireonline.com/tv/news/star-wars-andor-doesnt-use-volume-says-tony-gilroy-exclusive|text=Andor Doesn't Use Star Wars' Volume Video Wall: 'We're Old-School,' Says Tony Gilroy — Exclusive Image|author=Ben Travis|date=2022-01-08|work=[[Wikipedia:Empire (magazine)|''Empire'']]|archivedate=20220801153835}}</ref> while exterior scenes for the [[Aldhani dam]] were also filmed in Scotland, at the [[Wikipedia:Cruachan Power Station|Cruachan pumped storage hydro plant]].<ref name="Instagram-dam">{{Instagram|username=bencruachaninn|url=p/CiAmNIvK47K|name=Ben Cruachan Inn|date=2022-09-02|quote=Lots of excitement with the release of #starwars series #Andor|archivedate=20221013000727}}</ref> [[Ferrix]] was very expensive to create. Gilroy stated its "mental build" took two years.<ref name="Perfect Episode">{{WebCite|url=https://www.vanityfair.com/hollywood/2023/08/andor-secrets-awards-insider|text=''Andor'': Inside the Making of a Perfect Star Wars Episode|author=Anthony Breznican|date=2023-08-17|work=[[Wikipedia:Vanity Fair (magazine)|''Vanity Fair'']]|archivedate=20231024185917}}</ref> Filming wrapped in [[September]] 2021.<ref name="Diego Luna Andor Details">{{WebCite|url=https://deadline.com/2021/09/diego-luna-star-wars-andor-details-production-familiar-faces-1234845366|text=Diego Luna Says 'Star Wars: Andor' Has Finished Shooting, And To Expect "Familiar Faces"|author=Rosy Cordero|date=2021-09-27|work=[[Wikipedia:Deadline Hollywood|''Deadline'']]|archivedate=20210927235143}}</ref>

====Season two production====
=====Writers and Actors strikes=====
As part of the [[Wikipedia:2023 Writers Guild of America strike|2023 Writers Guild of America strike]], Gilroy ceased all services on ''Andor'' and did not return to the set.<ref name="Gilroy Ceases">{{WebCite|url=https://www.hollywoodreporter.com/tv/tv-news/andor-tony-gilroy-scabbing-accusations-strike-1235483978|text=Showrunner Tony Gilroy Ceases Producing Services on ‘Andor’ (Exclusive)|date=2023-05-09|work=[[Wikipedia:The Hollywood Reporter|''The Hollywood Reporter'']]|archivedate=20230730022000}}</ref> A few weeks before season two's UK shoot was to finish, ''[[Wikipedia:Deadline Hollywood|Deadline Hollywood]]'' opened an article by stating that filming on season two would pause as a result of the [[Wikipedia:2023 SAG-AFTRA strike|2023 SAG-AFTRA actors strike]]. Later in the piece, however, the article stated that, as per what ''Deadline'' had learned, the series was still being filmed at Pinewood Studios, but without actors who were part of SAG-AFTRA: American SAG-AFTRA actors had stopped work, as per the strike, while members of the [[Wikipedia:Equity (British trade union)|British Equity union]] remained. According to the report, actors who were part of Equity were warned of potential legal action should they stop work in solidarity with the American union.<ref name="Filming cuts short">{{WebCite|url=https://deadline.com/2023/07/andor-star-wars-disney-cut-short-sag-aftra-strike-1235442836|text=‘Andor’ Season 2 Shoot To Be Cut Short Amid SAG-AFTRA Strike|date=2023-07-20|work=[[Wikipedia:Deadline Hollywood|''Deadline'']]|archivedate=20230731151037}}</ref>

=====Post-strikes=====
